newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Profit-taking drags down Sri Lanka stocks.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking drags down Sri Lanka stocks.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed in negative territory for the first time in five weeks on continued profit-taking among stocks which had risen over 10 percent this year, brokers said.
The all share index closed 0.7 points down at 632.8. The last time the all share recorded a decline was on December 23.
Price declines led gains by 31 to 17. Walltile fell 1.50 rupees to 26.50, Ceylon Tobacco one rupee to 34.
"The index could fall to about 625 before buying returns, because profit-taking is among the same shares that took the index up," said Shafi Wahid a trader at CDIC Sasoon.
Trading was mainly in liquid shares like Dankotuwa Porcelain, Distilleries, Dockyard, Grain Elevators, Lanka Ceramic, Lanka Walltile, Lion Brewery, Merchant and Sampath.
Turnover was 26.6 million rupees on 992,913 shares, on local buying. Foreign buying was 7.4 milion rupees.
"We are buying, because we believe the downside is limited by forecasts of good growth in 1997," said A. Kathiravelupillai, of The Unit Trust Management Co.
Merchant Bank sought permission to make a bonus issue to an employee stock option trust, in a bid to improve profitability.
